A 2-day-old premature infant is evaluated for petechiae and persistent subcutaneous bruising. Delivery
was uncomplicated. The newborn’s vital signs include a temperature of 39.0°C (102.2°F), heart rate of
180/min, respiratory rate of 44/min, and blood pressure of 89/59 mm Hg. Physical examination reveals
dullness to percussion over the bilateral thoracic bases. A chest radiograph indicates pulmonary
hemorrhage. Laboratory findings are as follows: | Test | Result | | --- | --- | | Hemoglobin | 13.2 g/dL | |
Hematocrit | 41% | | Leukocyte count | 5,200/mm3 | | Neutrophils | 45% | | Bands | 3% | | Eosinophils |
1% | | Basophils | 0% | | Lymphocytes | 44% | | Monocytes | 2% | | Platelet count | 195,000/mm3 |
Coagulation studies show: | Test | Result | | --- | --- | | Partial thromboplastin time (activated) | 49 s | |
Prothrombin time/INR | 19 s/1.92 | | Reticulocyte count | 2.5% | | Thrombin time | < 2 s deviation from
control | What is the most likely underlying cause of this newborn's condition? Answer Choices: (A)
Platelet dysfunction due to prematurity (B) Congenital factor VII deficiency (C) Disseminated
intravascular coagulation (D) Liver immaturity with impaired clotting factor synthesis (E) Neonatal
alloimmune thrombocytopenia (F) Hemorrhagic disease of the newborn (G) Vitamin K deficiency (H)

Sepsis-induced coagulopathy (I) Hereditary thrombocytopathy (J) Autoimmune neonatal
thrombocytopenia
 A. Sepsis-induced coagulopathy
B. Autoimmune neonatal thrombocytopenia
